name: NETSCOUT AED — Surge in High-Confidence Threat Activity Against a Bank Internet Service
description:
Attacker objective
Compromise an internet-facing banking service through a coordinated exploitation or botnet campaign — many distinct high-reputation threat sources (active exploiters, botnet C2, named exploit tooling) targeting the same service in a short window.

Attack logic
The edge appliance blocks inbound traffic from sources flagged by threat intelligence as active exploiters, botnet command-and-control, or named exploit campaigns. A surge in the number of distinct such sources targeting one protected service — well above the steady background of internet scanning — indicates a coordinated, targeted campaign against that service.

Why this detection works
Counting distinct high-confidence threat sources per protected service over a short window separates a coordinated campaign from the constant low background of individual scanners the appliance blocks.

False positives
A general internet-wide scanning wave or botnet sweep that incidentally raises counts across many services (not targeted); a threat-intel feed false-positive.

Tuning
Set the distinct-source surge threshold above the observed background; prioritise surges against internet-banking and webmail services; correlate with F5 WAF attack volume against the same service.

Required telemetry
NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense (CEF): Threat Name (deviceCustomString6), Threat Category (cs7), Protection Group (deviceCustomString2), source.ip (external threat source), destination.ip (bank service).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. deviceCustomString2 = the targeted service; review the threat names/categories and the distinct source IPs and their geography/ASN.
2. A surge of exploiter/C2 sources against internet banking or webmail can precede a real intrusion attempt — raise monitoring and correlate with F5 WAF and FortiGate/PAN-OS for the same service.
3. Confirm whether any of the campaign traffic was not blocked (reached the app).
false_positives: A general internet-wide scanning wave or botnet sweep that incidentally raises counts across many services (not targeted); a threat-intel feed false-positive.
query: observer.vendor:"NETSCOUT" and (cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6:("Botnet Command and Control" or "Active Exploiters" or "MOVEit Transfer" or "CnC Other" or "Eleven11 Botnet" or "DNS Flood") or cef.extensions.cs7:"Command and Control")

name: NETSCOUT AED — Volumetric DDoS Surge Against a Bank Internet Service
description:
Attacker objective
Deny availability of an internet-facing banking service (internet/mobile banking, webmail, corporate portal) by flooding it — TCP SYN/ICMP flood, fragmentation, rate abuse, or malformed-protocol attacks.

Attack logic
The edge DDoS-defense appliance mitigates volumetric and protocol attacks against the bank's protected internet services. A short-window surge of these mitigation events against one protected service, well above the steady background the appliance handles, indicates an active DDoS attack rather than routine background floods.

Why this detection works
Aggregating DDoS-mitigation events per protected service over a short window separates a genuine volumetric attack from the low, steady rate of background floods the appliance blocks continuously.

False positives
A legitimate traffic spike (marketing campaign, product launch) misread as a flood; a scheduled load test against a protected service.

Tuning
Set the per-service surge threshold above the observed background rate; allowlist scheduled load tests; correlate with the F5/FortiGate view of the same service and with any upstream cloud-signaling.

Required telemetry
NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense (CEF): cef.device.event_class_id (DDoS mitigation classes), Protection Group (deviceCustomString2), source.ip (attacker), destination.ip (bank service), destination.port.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. deviceCustomString2 = the targeted bank service; review the attack type (event_class_id), source geography/ASN and destination port.
2. Confirm whether the service is degraded; if so, engage DDoS response and upstream cloud-signaling.
3. Correlate with F5/FortiGate for the same public service and with any customer-impact reports.
false_positives: A legitimate traffic spike (marketing campaign, product launch) misread as a flood; a scheduled load test against a protected service.
query: observer.vendor:"NETSCOUT" and cef.device.event_class_id:("TCP SYN Flood Detection" or "ICMP Flood Detection" or "Rate-based Blocking" or "TCP Connection Limiting" or "Fragment Detection" or "Block Malformed DNS Traffic" or "Malformed HTTP Filtering")

name: Potential Denial of Service (DoS) Attack
description: This rule detects an anomalously high volume of trafficoriginating from a single source IP address. A large number of requests in a short period can indicate an attempt For a DOS attack, rendering it unavailable for legitimate traffic.

name: Potential Destribution Denial of Service (DDoS) Attack
description: This rule detects an anomalously high volume of traffic originating from a Multiple source IP address targeting a specific Service. A large number of requests in a short period can indicate an attempt For a DDoS attack, rendering it unavailable for legitimate traffic.
